name: Western Australian Botanic Garden
reason: Rule 3, part of a larger spot: the garden lies inside Kings Park, and Wikivoyage Perth/Downtown lists the two together as one listing ('Kings Park & Botanic Gardens'). Keep it as one with Kings Park, not as a second spot.
objection: Lonely Planet's 'Top things to do in Perth' gives the garden its own entry (3,000 plants, the 750-year-old boab). If the Kings Park spot is kept, its name or bio should cover the Botanic Garden.

name: Mount Eliza
reason: Rule 3, duplicate of Kings Park: Mount Eliza is the ridge Kings Park sits on, and its summit lookout (Kaarta Gar-up) is part of the Kings Park visit. No visitor source lists it apart from the park.
objection: The Kings Park lookout over the city and river is one of Perth's best-known views; that belongs in the Kings Park bio.

name: Bali Memorial
reason: Rule 3, minor memorial: a monument inside Kings Park. No counted source names it, and it is a short look within a larger spot.
objection: It is one of the memorials a Kings Park walk passes.

name: Edith Dircksey Cowan Memorial
reason: Rule 3, minor memorial: a clock-tower memorial at the Kings Park entrance. No counted source names it as somewhere to go.
objection: It is a heritage-listed landmark at the park gates, but a ten-minute look at most.

name: Perth Cultural Centre
reason: Rule 3, duplicate wrapper: the precinct is the setting of the Art Gallery of WA, WA Museum Boola Bardip and PICA, which are judged as spots in their own right. Keep those, and mention the precinct in their bios.
objection: Wikivoyage Perth/Northbridge and Tourism WA both list the Cultural Centre as a precinct, and it is a real place to spend a day. Keep it only if the owner prefers the precinct over its venues.

name: Western Australian Museum
reason: Rule 1, obvious draw: Wikivoyage Perth/Northbridge lists it (daily 9AM-5PM), and Lonely Planet calls WA Museum Boola Bardip 'an unmissable attraction'. The state museum, eight permanent galleries, hours of visit. Name it WA Museum Boola Bardip (the Perth site), not the organisation.
objection: 'Western Australian Museum' is also the name of the statewide organisation with sites in Fremantle, Albany, Geraldton and Kalgoorlie; the spot must be the Perth building only.

name: Perth Institute of Contemporary Arts
reason: Rule 1, two counted sources: Wikivoyage Perth/Northbridge lists it, and Visit Perth (the City of Perth's visitor site) lists PICA as a venue with year-round exhibitions in one of Australia's largest exhibition spaces. Rule 2: free galleries, Tue-Sun.
objection: It is next to the Art Gallery of WA in the same precinct, and its programme is rotating contemporary work that a general visitor may skip. A reviewer could call it secondary to AGWA.

name: Chinatown Perth
reason: Rule 2 and 3: a small precinct of Asian groceries and restaurants with a gate on Roe Street, inside Northbridge. It is shops and restaurants, and part of the Northbridge candidate; keep it as one with Northbridge (its bio can mention Chinatown).
objection: Wikivoyage Perth/Northbridge, Visit Perth and a Destination Perth blog all name it, so it has more source support than most rejects.

name: Northbridge
reason: For: Wikivoyage gives it its own district page and Tourism WA has a 'places' page for it: Perth's arts, dining and nightlife quarter, with street art, Chinatown and the Cultural Centre.
objection: Against: a neighbourhood whose daytime draws (the Art Gallery, WA Museum, PICA) are separate spots, leaving restaurants and bars, which are not spots on their own (rule 2). Keep only if the owner wants districts as spots.

name: Swan Bells
reason: Rule 1 and 2: Wikivoyage Perth/Downtown lists the Bell Tower at Barrack Square (go inside, see and hear the 18 bells, river and city views from the observation deck). A paid attraction with six levels and bell-ringing experiences.
objection: One counted source only, and Wikivoyage notes locals see it as controversial. Tourism WA has no listing for it that I could find.

name: Perth Observatory
reason: For: Tourism WA lists it (WA's oldest observatory, at Bickley, with night sky tours, a museum and Sunday day tours), and the observatory's own site confirms public tours.
objection: Against rule 4: you can only visit on a booked tour (night tours Fri-Sun, day tours Sunday afternoons), so it is not there whenever you arrive. One counted source.

name: Old Mill
reason: Rule 1, two counted sources: Wikivoyage Perth/The Suburbs and Tourism WA both list it. The 1835 windmill at Mill Point by the Narrows Bridge is the oldest surviving colonial structure in the Perth area, with grounds open daily.
objection: The mill and miller's cottage interiors open only on limited days (Wikivoyage: Tue-Fri 10-4, weekend afternoons; other guides say fewer), so on many days it is an exterior look of under half an hour.

name: Perth Zoo
reason: Rule 1, obvious draw: Wikivoyage Perth/The Suburbs lists it, Visit Perth lists it (open daily 9-5), and Tourism WA names it among WA's animal encounters. A zoo open since 1898, a half day or more.
objection: Little: it is a city zoo rather than a uniquely Western Australian sight, but it is the state's main zoo.

name: WACA Ground
reason: Rule 2 and 4: a cricket ground you visit for matches, and the WACA's own site says its museum and ground tours are temporarily closed during the ground improvement works. Wikivoyage mentions it only as a home ground, not as a See listing.
objection: 68,000 page views and a Visit Perth venue page; a rebuilt museum is planned, so it may qualify again once the museum and tours reopen.

name: Aviation Heritage Museum
reason: Rule 1: Tourism WA lists it (civilian and military aviation displays, about 30 aircraft including a Lancaster, guided tours) at Bull Creek. Rule 2: open year-round; the museum's own site suggests an hour or two.
objection: One counted source only, and it is a specialist museum in the suburbs; a reviewer could send it to review.

name: Western Australian Rail Transport Museum
reason: For: a real museum of WA rolling stock at Bassendean run by Rail Heritage WA (locomotives from 1881's Katie to the first mainline diesel), with paid entry. Wikipedia cites a Tourism WA listing.
objection: Against: I found no counted source directly (only the operator, Wikipedia and blogs), and it opens only on Wednesdays and Sundays (rule 4: not there whenever you arrive).

name: Scitech
reason: Rule 1: Tourism WA and Visit Perth both list it (science discovery centre with six interactive galleries and Australasia's largest planetarium, open daily 9.30-4). Rule 2: a paid half-day attraction.
objection: Aimed at children; a reviewer could argue adults without kids would not go out of their way for it.

name: Museum of Perth
reason: Rule 1: no counted source names it (only Wikipedia's museum category and its own events pages). It moved to the Bon Marché Arcade in 2024, and I found no current hours.
objection: A small private city-history museum that may well be open; if Visit Perth lists it, it could come back as a review.

name: The Nostalgia Box
reason: Rule 1: I found no counted source (only Wikipedia, blogs and ticket sites).
objection: A paid, hands-on video-game console museum (100+ consoles, many playable) in West Perth that is popular with families; a Visit Perth or Tourism WA listing would make it a review.

name: Berndt Museum of Anthropology
reason: Rule 3, duplicate of Lawrence Wilson Art Gallery: its exhibitions are shown in the Janet Holmes à Court Gallery inside the Lawrence Wilson Art Gallery. No counted source names it.
objection: A significant Aboriginal and Pacific collection; if the gallery were kept, the Berndt shows would belong in its bio.

name: Lawrence Wilson Art Gallery
reason: Rule 1: no counted source found (only UWA's own pages and art-listing sites); a university gallery open Tue-Sat.
objection: Free, Australia's first purpose-built university art museum, and it houses the Berndt Museum collection; a Visit Perth listing would make it a review.

name: Perth Gaol
reason: Rule 3, part of a larger spot: the 1856 Old Gaol is part of WA Museum Boola Bardip; Wikivoyage describes it under the museum's listing ('The Old Gaol building at the rear houses colonial artefacts').
objection: It is a distinct heritage building, but you visit it as part of the museum.

name: Old Central Fire Station
reason: For: Visit Perth lists it as the DFES Education and Heritage Centre (fire brigade history, vintage fire trucks, free) in the 1901 fire station on Murray Street. One counted source.
objection: Against: open only Tue-Thu and the first and third Saturdays (rule 4), aimed at families, and a short visit; one source for a marginal stop.

name: Old Perth Boys School
reason: Rule 2: the 1854 school is now a Curtin University venue; public access is limited to occasional exhibitions and events. No counted source names it.
objection: A National Trust heritage building on St Georges Terrace that is sometimes open.

name: Old Swan Brewery
reason: Rule 2: the former brewery is now apartments and a restaurant; seen from the road or riverside path only. No counted source names it as somewhere to go.
objection: A well-known riverside landmark below Kings Park, and it is in Wikipedia's Perth tourist category.

name: Old Kerosene Store
reason: Rule 1 and 2: no counted source names it, and no public access is confirmed; a heritage building seen from outside.
objection: Listed in Wikipedia's Perth tourist category.

name: Tranby House
reason: For: a National Trust house museum (Peninsula Farm, built 1839, one of WA's oldest surviving houses) at Maylands, open to the public with a guide, set in riverside gardens with tearooms next door.
objection: Against: I found no counted source (only Wikipedia, aumuseums, Hello Perth and Weekend Notes; the National Trust site blocks scripts), and it opens only a few days a week (Fri-Sun by the latest listing).

name: Halliday House
reason: Rule 1 and 2: a heritage house in Bassendean with no counted source and no confirmed public opening.
objection: Has a Wikipedia article.

name: Schmidt-Lademann House
reason: Rule 1 and 2: a private heritage house in Wembley Downs; no counted source and no public access.
objection: Has a Wikipedia article and an OSM node; neither counts.

name: The Cloisters
reason: Rule 2: an 1858 school building on St Georges Terrace now used as offices; exterior only. No counted source names it.
objection: A heritage landmark on a guide's walking route could qualify, but no counted source names it.

name: Government House, Perth
reason: For: Tourism WA and Visit Perth both list it; the 1864 Governor's residence has 3.2 ha of gardens open to the public, and the house opens on a few open days a year.
objection: Against rule 2 and 4: the house itself is exterior-only except on open days, and the gardens open only Tue-Thu 12-2pm, so most visitors see it from the street.

name: Barracks Arch
reason: For: Wikivoyage Perth/Downtown lists it as a See item, and Tourism WA has an attraction page: the 1866 arch at the end of St Georges Terrace that is all that remains of the Pensioner Guard barracks.
objection: Against rule 2 and 3: a free-standing arch you look at from the street for a few minutes, in front of Parliament House; a photo stop, not a half-hour visit.

name: Wireless Hill Park
reason: Rule 1: Tourism WA lists it (38 ha of bushland with spring wildflowers and orchids, a hilltop lookout over Perth and the Swan River, and the Wireless Hill Museum in the old radio station). Rule 2: walks, lookout and museum fill an hour or more.
objection: One counted source; the City of Melville and Bushland Perth pages are local, and the museum opens only on limited days.

name: Lake Monger
reason: Rule 1, two counted sources: Tourism WA lists Galup (Lake Monger) as the home of Perth's black swans, with boardwalks and a 3.5 km lake circuit, and Wikivoyage Perth names it among Perth's parks; Lonely Planet has a point-of-interest entry. A second-tier stop for swans and the city skyline.
objection: It is a suburban lake park mainly used by locals for walking and jogging, close to the 'ordinary suburban park' negative benchmark.

name: Bold Park
reason: Rule 1: managed by the Botanic Gardens and Parks Authority, which publishes a visitor map and runs free guided walks; Trails WA lists the Reabold Hill Summit Boardwalk (the highest point on the coastal plain, views to the ocean, Perth and the Darling Scarp); Wikivoyage Perth names it among Perth's parks. Rule 2: the Zamia Trail (5.1 km) and lookouts.
objection: An urban bushland park that is mostly used by locals; a reviewer could send it to review.

name: Hyde Park, Perth
reason: Rule 3 and the 'ordinary suburban park' benchmark: a pleasant inner-city park with lakes, lawns and a playground, used by locals for picnics; no guide singles out something to see.
objection: Tourism WA does have a listing for it (twin lakes, Aboriginal heritage site), and it has 7,000 page views.

name: Langley Park
reason: Rule 2 and 4: a riverside lawn in the city used for events and as an overflow car park; no counted source names it as somewhere to go.
objection: Has a Wikipedia article and is a well-known riverside open space.

name: Supreme Court Gardens
reason: Rule 2 and 4: small city gardens mainly used as an events venue; no counted source.
objection: Central and pleasant, beside the Swan Bells and Elizabeth Quay walk.

name: Queens Gardens
reason: Rule 3, ordinary city park: small gardens in East Perth with a Peter Pan statue; no counted source.
objection: A pretty Victorian-style garden that some walking guides pass.

name: Stirling Gardens
reason: Rule 3, ordinary city park: no counted source names the gardens. The 'Kangaroos in the City' bronzes that Wikivoyage lists are nearby, a separate candidate if anything.
objection: Central gardens on the way between Barrack Square and the city, with the kangaroo sculptures beside them.

name: Peace Memorial Rose Garden
reason: Rule 1 and 3: a local rose garden in Nedlands with no counted source; a short look.
objection: Has a Wikipedia article and OSM entry.

name: East Perth Cemeteries
reason: Rule 1 and 4: I found no counted source (only the National Trust's own site, Wikipedia and a paid walking tour), and the grounds open only on Sundays 2-4pm.
objection: WA's first colonial burial ground (1829), run by the National Trust with guided tours; a Visit Perth listing would make it a review.

name: Wellington Square
reason: Rule 3, ordinary city park: a city park used for sport and events; no counted source.
objection: Recently renamed Moort-ak Waadiny and redeveloped; has a Wikipedia article.

name: Russell Square
reason: Rule 3, ordinary city park: a small Northbridge square; no counted source.
objection: Has a Wikipedia article.

name: Solidarity Park
reason: Rule 3, ordinary city park: a small park beside Parliament House known for protests; no counted source.
objection: Has a Wikipedia article.

name: Sir James Mitchell Park
reason: For: Tourism WA's 'South Perth Foreshore' listing, which names Sir James Mitchell Park, calls it an iconic tourist destination with the best panoramic views of the Perth skyline across the Swan River.
objection: Against: a riverside lawn and playgrounds used by locals; it is the view rather than the park that is the draw. If kept, name it South Perth Foreshore and check it is not the same place as another candidate (the Old Mill and Perth Zoo are on the same foreshore).

name: Banyowla Regional Park
reason: Rule 1: no counted source; regional bushland on the metro edge that no guide mentions (the COVERAGE 'regional park beside a city' case).
objection: Bushland on the Darling Scarp with walk trails.

name: Yellagonga Regional Park
reason: For: the DBCA visitor page (managing agency) describes Lake Joondalup and Lake Goollelal with walking and cycling circuits, birdlife and settler-era ruins.
objection: Against: DBCA writes a page for every regional park; it is suburban parkland that DBCA itself calls 'a leafy oasis in the heart of suburbia', and no guide names it (close to the 'regional park beside a city that no guide mentions' rule).

name: Canning River Regional Park
reason: Rule 3, local reserve: six kilometres of riverside bushland with walking, canoeing and picnics; only the DBCA page names it, and it is a local recreation park rather than a place visitors travel for.
objection: DBCA mentions Woodloes Homestead and the Kent Street Weir; a guide naming either would make it a review.

name: Jandakot Regional Park
reason: Rule 3, local reserve: banksia woodland with bridle trails; only the DBCA page, which pitches it to horse riders.
objection: Spring wildflowers.

name: Beeliar Regional Park
reason: Rule 3, local reserve: a chain of 19 suburban wetlands south of Perth; only the DBCA page names it, with nothing specific to go to.
objection: 3,400 ha of wetlands with birdlife; individual lakes might be judged on their own.

name: Wungong Regional Park
reason: Rule 3, local reserve: Darling Range bushland around Wungong Dam; only the DBCA page names it.
objection: Wildflowers and fairy wrens at the dam.

name: Rockingham Lakes Regional Park
reason: For: the DBCA page names two real draws, the Lake Richmond thrombolites ('a star attraction of the park') and Cape Peron, its hub, with snorkelling, viewing platforms and a coastal walk.
objection: Against: an umbrella area; its draws are better judged as places of their own (Cape Peron, Lake Richmond), and a park-wide pin would duplicate them.

name: Adventure World
reason: Rule 1 and 2: Wikivoyage Perth/The Suburbs lists it (Bibra Lake theme and water park, rides and waterslides). WA's main theme park, a full day; a seasonal venue (Sept-April) is fine under rule 4.
objection: No Tourism WA page found; it is closed through the winter months.

name: Caversham Wildlife Park
reason: Rule 1: Tourism WA lists it (the largest private collection of native animals in WA, about 200 species, in Whiteman Park), with hand-feeding kangaroos and koala encounters. Rule 2: open daily, a half-day visit.
objection: One counted source; it is inside Whiteman Park, so if Whiteman Park is kept the two must not share a pin.

name: Cohunu Koala Park
reason: Rule 1, two counted sources: Tourism WA lists it (family-run sanctuary at Byford since 1972) and Frommer's has a guide entry (hand-feed kangaroos, see koalas, wombats and dingoes, walk-through aviary). Rule 2: paid, open daily.
objection: A 2016 Zoochat report called it poor value, and Frommer's koala-holding claim needs checking.

name: West Australian Reptile Park
reason: For: the Swan Valley's tourism site lists it (pythons, venomous snakes, crocodiles, wombats and dingoes, with presentations) at Henley Brook. Rule 2: paid wildlife park.
objection: Against: one counted source for a small private park, and Caversham Wildlife Park nearby covers the same wildlife-park draw better.

name: Armadale Reptile Centre
reason: Rule 1-2: Tourism WA attraction listing (westernaustralia.com/en/attraction/armadale-reptile-centre) and Experience Perth Hills '10 must-visit nature and wildlife experiences' both name it; open six days with paid entry, 50+ reptile species plus kangaroos and dingoes, a 1-2 hr visit.
objection: A small suburban wildlife centre (786 views); friend test says 'only if nearby with kids'. Closed Wednesdays outside school holidays.

name: Kanyana Wildlife Rehabilitation Centre
reason: For: Experience Perth Hills names it among the hills' 10 must-visit wildlife experiences (Discovery Tours, nocturnal tours; bilbies and woylies); Destination Perth listed it. Against rule 2: it is a working wildlife hospital visitors can enter only on booked tours on Thursdays and Sundays, not whenever they arrive.
objection: Tour-only access two days a week, bookings essential; one counted source for a marginal place.

name: Perth's Outback Splash
reason: Rule 1-2, 4: Tourism WA attraction listing ('one of WA's top outdoor entertainment destinations') and the Swan Valley tourism listing name it; a water park with 9 slides, mazes and mini-golf, a half-day visit. Seasonal venue (Sept-April), which rule 4 allows.
objection: A family amusement venue mainly for locals' children; closed May-August since 2024.

name: Ocean Reef Marina
reason: Rule 1-2: no visitor source names it; it is a boat marina still under development (the coastal pool and beach were due to open in 2026, not confirmed open). A marina is a local facility, not a visitor draw today.
objection: Government expects it to become a 'key attraction like Hillarys Boat Harbour' once the pool opens; re-look when it does.

name: Sunset Heritage Precinct
reason: Rule 1-2: no visitor source; the former Sunset Hospital site has 'remained largely unused since 1995', with only open grounds and picnic facilities, and the state is seeking redevelopment proposals (EOI closed Aug 2026).
objection: 2903 page views and riverside grounds open since 2016; if redeveloped as an arts/cultural precinct it could qualify later.

name: Sunset Coast
reason: Rule 3: a tourism-brand stretch of coastline (Perth's northern beaches), not a single place; its beaches (Cottesloe, Scarborough, Trigg etc.) are judged as candidates in their own right. No counted source names it as somewhere to go as one spot.
objection: The name does appear in Perth tourism marketing; it could serve as name evidence for a coast grouping, but not as a pinned spot.

name: Sikh Heritage Cremation Site
reason: Rule 3: a minor heritage marker on the Australian Sikh Heritage Trail; no visitor source, 0 views, nothing to do for half an hour.
objection: Culturally significant to a community heritage trail.

name: Mundaring Sculpture Park
reason: Rule 1-2: Tourism WA attraction listing (Mundaring Community Sculpture Park: sculptures by eight WA artists, the Moodae-ring acoustic sculpture) and Experience Perth Hills town guides name it; sculpture walk, playground, trailhead of the Munda Biddi and Railway Reserves Heritage Trails. Name in the app should be 'Mundaring Community Sculpture Park'.
objection: Essentially a small town park with a playground; the Saturday farmers' market there is not part of the spot (rule 4). Could be argued a local park (review).

name: Wyola Wreck
reason: Rule 1-3: no counted source as a visitor place; the stern frame of a tug buried in the sand at CY O'Connor Beach, North Coogee, plus a shallow dive site in the WA Museum's wreck notes. A short look or a specialist dive, not a general draw.
objection: WA Museum (an agency) documents it as a shallow dive with marine growth; a quirky beach relic that could support a CY O'Connor Beach spot's bio.

name: Bell Cottage Ruin
reason: Rule 2: the state heritage entry says the ruin is fenced, inaccessible to the public and obscured from view by trees; heritage register only, no visitor source.
objection: State Register-listed, part of the East Rockingham Heritage Precinct.

name: Samuel Ferguson's Cottage
reason: Rule 1-3: only Wikipedia/heritage listings; a cottage (ruin) that is one numbered stop on the Toodyay Pioneer Heritage Trail, a minor part of a larger walk with nothing to do for half an hour.
objection: It is a named stop of a heritage trail, which can qualify a heritage building; but the trail is the draw, not this ruin.

name: Mahogany Inn
reason: Brief rule: accommodation venue (a historic inn operating as a B&B/function venue); no visitor source names it as a sight.
objection: Historic 1840s inn building in the Perth Hills.

name: Redemptorist Monastery
reason: Rule 1-2 (church rule): a working monastery and church in North Perth; no visitor source names anything to see or do there (no interior tour, art or guide mention). Heritage register and Wikipedia only.
objection: 1517 page views; an imposing heritage building, but only seen from the street as far as any source says.

name: Kuljak Island
reason: Rule 1-3: an artificial island on a capped former rubbish tip off Ascot Waters with footpaths; no visitor source (the Swan River kangaroo island visitors go to is Heirisson Island, a different place downstream). A local riverside reserve.
objection: Has walking paths and is a backdrop to Peninsula Farm (Tranby House) across the river.

name: E Shed Markets
reason: Rule 4: a market that trades only Friday to Sunday (and public holidays), not daily.
objection: Wikivoyage mentions it in passing near the Rottnest ferry wharf; it is a fixed venue at Victoria Quay.

name: Peninsula Farm
reason: For: the National Trust heritage house and farm (formerly Tranby House, now 'Peninsula Farm at Wu-rut Woorat', 1839) on the Swan River; Hello Perth visitor guide names it, the house is open with volunteer guides and an entry fee, the grounds daily, with a cafe. Likely the same place as any 'Tranby House' candidate: keep as one under its current name.
objection: The house opens only Friday and Saturday; one visitor source; a suburban heritage house museum, 'only if nearby'.

name: Perth Hills
reason: Rule 1: Wikivoyage district 'Perth/The Hills' and the Experience Perth Hills tourism brand name it; it is a region (John Forrest NP, Mundaring Weir, Lesmurdie Falls, Kalamunda) — name evidence for the proposer (a destination or grouping), not a single pinned spot.
objection: An area, not a place: it cannot be a spot itself; the proposer must decide whether it is a destination or whether its parts are Perth spots.

name: WA Shipwrecks Museum
reason: Rule 1-2: Wikivoyage Fremantle See listing, Visit Fremantle top free things and Tourism WA's Fremantle page all name it; free museum with the Batavia timbers, 1-2 hr visit.
objection: Weak score only because it has no article of its own under this title (Wikipedia: 'Western Australian Shipwrecks Museum'); none on substance.

name: Western Australian Maritime Museum
reason: Rule 1-2: Wikivoyage Fremantle See listing and Tourism WA's Fremantle page; museum with Australia II and the HMAS Ovens submarine tour, open daily.
objection: None of substance; 0 views is a title mismatch with its Wikipedia article.

name: HMAS Ovens
reason: Rule 3: duplicate/part of the Western Australian Maritime Museum: the submarine is toured as part of a museum ticket on Victoria Quay; keep it as one with the museum and mention it in the museum's bio.
objection: 4800 page views and a separate tour ticket; a vessel-as-attraction could stand alone, but it sits beside the museum and is sold with it.

name: Round House
reason: Rule 1-2: Wikivoyage Fremantle See listing and Visit Fremantle's top free things; WA's oldest public building (1831), a free small museum on Arthur Head with views over Bathers Bay.
objection: A short visit (30 min) on a small headland; strong enough with two sources.

name: Whalers' Tunnel
reason: Rule 3: part of the Round House (it runs under it on Arthur Head to Bathers Beach); keep as one with the Round House and mention the tunnel in its bio.
objection: Wikivoyage gives it its own See listing as a self-guided display.

name: Cantonment Hill
reason: For: Wikivoyage Fremantle See listing ('a terrific view of Fremantle Harbour'), free lookout beside the Army Museum. Against: one counted source and a short viewpoint visit; the signal station building is not open; Visit Fremantle points visitors to Monument Hill instead.
objection: Marginal per the one-source-and-short-visit rule; may be best mentioned in the Army Museum's bio.

name: Army Museum of Western Australia
reason: Rule 1-2: Wikivoyage Fremantle See listing with hours and prices; a military museum in the old Artillery Barracks, 1-2 hr visit.
objection: Opens only Wed-Fri and Sun, 10:30-3; one counted source.

name: The Moores Building
reason: For: Wikivoyage Do listing: a contemporary art gallery with six exhibition spaces in the West End, free entry. Against rule 3: Wikivoyage itself calls it part of Fremantle Arts Centre; a small gallery whose shows come and go.
objection: Part-of signal: if Fremantle Arts Centre is kept, this is a near-duplicate; could also be folded into the West End spot.

name: Bathers Beach
reason: Rule 1-2: Visit Fremantle top free things (Manjaree / Bathers Beach) and Tourism WA's Fremantle page name it; a swimming beach below the Round House with a licensed area on the sand and the Bathers Beach art precinct.
objection: Small town beach; near-duplicate risk with the Round House/Fishing Boat Harbour precinct.

name: South Beach
reason: Rule 1-2: Wikivoyage Fremantle Do listing and Visit Fremantle's free things ('much-loved' family swimming beach with BBQs, shade, sauna). NOTE: the candidate's coordinates (25.78, -80.14) are South Beach, Miami: the pin must be re-resolved in South Fremantle (about -32.076, 115.751 per Wikivoyage).
objection: A suburban family beach; second tier.

name: Fisherman's Wharf
reason: Rule 1-2: keep as 'Fishing Boat Harbour' (Fremantle Fishing Boat Harbour), the place Visit Fremantle (top 10 free, #9), Tourism WA's Fremantle page and Wikivoyage ('Esplanade and Boat harbour') name: boardwalks, working fishing fleet, the Bon Scott statue, fish and chips. 'Fisherman's Wharf' is only Cicerello's outdoor seating there.
objection: Partly a dining strip (rule: restaurants alone fail); the Bon Scott statue and boardwalk carry it.

name: Cappuccino Strip
reason: For: Fremantle's famous cafe street (South Terrace), named by Wikivoyage (walking area), Visit Fremantle ('the famous Cappuccino Strip', a stop on the Fremantle Discovery Trail) and Tourism WA. Against rule 2: it is a strip of cafes and restaurants; a street of businesses, which the bar fails unless the street itself is the recognised attraction.
objection: Could be judged a recognised landmark street (keep) or folded into a Fremantle town/West End spot.

name: Fremantle West End
reason: Rule 1-2: Wikivoyage ('West End' walking area), Visit Fremantle (heritage-listed West End, galleries, Discovery Trail) and Tourism WA name it: Australia's largest intact Victorian-era port streetscape, walked for an hour or more.
objection: A district rather than a single place; overlaps the Round House, Shipwrecks Museum and Moores Building it contains. If Fremantle itself is a destination, the proposer may fold it into the description.

name: Esplanade Park, Fremantle
reason: For: Tourism WA's Fremantle page (Ferris wheel at Esplanade Park) and Visit Fremantle (Esplanade Reserve on the Discovery Trail, skate park, playground). Against rule 3 / Leave out: an urban park under Norfolk pines whose draws are a seasonal-ish tourist wheel and a youth skate park; 'an ordinary park' negative benchmark.
objection: Two counted sources name it, but as a place to pass through on the way to the Fishing Boat Harbour.

name: Fremantle Walking Tours and Trails
reason: A spot is a place: a set of tours and self-guided trails, not a place; the places they visit (West End, Round House, Prison) are their own candidates.
objection: Visit Fremantle promotes the Discovery Trail; it belongs in Fremantle's tips.

name: Rottnest Island
reason: Rule 1: Wikivoyage park page and Tourism WA's Rottnest Island page; car-free island reserve with quokkas, beaches and snorkelling, Perth's top day trip (81,891 views). Area: the proposer decides destination vs spot.
objection: None on inclusion; only the destination-vs-spot question.

name: Wadjemup Lighthouse
reason: Rule 1-2: Wikivoyage Rottnest See listing; stop on every island tour (Rottnest Express Grand Island Tour), on the island's highest point with views; lighthouse tours run by the island authority.
objection: Operators say you can't always enter; a short stop. Part of the island, but a distinct named sight.

name: The Basin
reason: Rule 1-2: Rottnest's best-known swimming beach: the Rottnest Island Authority's beach guide (rottnestisland.com, blocked to scripts) and the ferry operators' guides rank it first; patrolled in summer, shallow reef pool. Second-tier beach a source names: keep.
objection: No unblocked counted source opened (rottnestisland.com returns a bot wall; Wikivoyage Rottnest names beaches only generally); check the RIA page in a browser.

name: Cathedral Rocks
reason: Rule 1-2: purpose-built viewing platform over a New Zealand fur seal colony at Rottnest's West End, a stop on island tours (Rottnest Express Grand Island Tour, opened) and in Rottnest Island Authority material. NOTE: the candidate's coordinates (-77.85, 162.6) are Cathedral Rocks, Antarctica: re-resolve near Cape Vlamingh (about -32.02, 115.45).
objection: Short look (15-30 min) and the second counted source is an operator; could be folded into a West End/Cape Vlamingh spot.

name: Armstrong Bay
reason: For: (Little) Armstrong Bay is repeatedly named by Rottnest guides as one of the island's best beginner snorkelling bays. Against: sources found are ferry operators, not counted; one of dozens of Rottnest bays; the candidate is 'Armstrong Bay' while guides name 'Little Armstrong Bay'.
objection: Rottnest has 60+ bays; listing many dilutes the island; one beach spot (The Basin) may suffice.

name: Thomson Bay
reason: For: the island's main settlement where the ferries land, with the shops, bakery, museum and accommodation; visitors base there (town rule). Against rule 3: it is the arrival point of Rottnest Island rather than a separate draw, and no counted source names it as somewhere to go in itself.
objection: Likely a near-duplicate of Rottnest Island; useful only if the island becomes a destination with the settlement as its gateway spot.

name: Oliver Hill Battery
reason: Rule 1-2: Wikivoyage Rottnest See ('wartime remnants, such as old barracks and cannons') and the island's guided Oliver Hill guns-and-tunnels tour (Rottnest Express Grand Island Tour, opened): restored 9.2-inch WWII guns and tunnels, a 45-60 min tour, reached by the heritage train.
objection: Tour-led access; the second counted source is an operator, the authority's own page was bot-blocked.

name: Rottnest Quokkas
reason: A spot is a place / rule 3: the quokkas live across the whole island; they are Rottnest Island's draw, not a separate place. Duplicate of Rottnest Island (mention in its bio).
objection: The quokka is the island's headline experience; but there is no single place to pin.

name: Swan Valley
reason: Rule 1: Wikivoyage district 'Perth/Swan_Valley', Wikivoyage Perth and Tourism WA (Swan Valley under Perth and Surrounds); wine, brewery and food region. Area: name evidence for the proposer (destination or spot).
objection: An area, not a single place; the proposer decides.

name: Guildford
reason: Town rule: Wikivoyage Swan Valley See listing ('one of WA's oldest settlements', whole town a heritage locality, James St) and Perth page (antique stores); the gateway to the Swan Valley.
objection: A suburb now absorbed into Perth; its draw is a heritage streetscape, a 1-2 hr wander.

name: Swan Valley Visitor Centre
reason: Rule 2: a visitor information centre, not an attraction; the museum it is attached to (Guildford courthouse/gaol) would be judged on its own.
objection: Wikivoyage gives it a See listing and notes the attached museum.

name: All Saints Anglican Church, Henley Brook
reason: For: Wikivoyage Swan Valley See listing names it as Western Australia's oldest church (1841) with a historic cemetery, grounds and a walk to the Swan River; entry free (church rule: a landmark a guide singles out). Against: one counted source and a short visit; still a working parish church.
objection: One source plus a 20-30 minute stop; marginal by rule.

name: Houghtons Wines
reason: Brief winery rule: the Houghton name has left the Swan Valley — the winery was sold to Oakover in 2019 and the site is now Nikola Estate; Wikivoyage's link is marked dead. Under this name it is not a place to go.
objection: The 1836 estate is WA's oldest winery; if the owner wants it, judge 'Nikola Estate' as its own candidate (a landmark estate could qualify).

name: Oakover Wines
reason: Brief winery rule: one of dozens of Swan Valley cellar doors in a bare Wikivoyage list, no source singles it out as a destination.
objection: Large family estate with restaurant; but no guide singles it out.

name: Jarrah Ridge
reason: Brief winery rule: a cellar door in a bare Wikivoyage list, not singled out as a destination.
objection: None beyond the list mention.

name: Sitella Wines
reason: Brief winery rule: a cellar door in a bare Wikivoyage list, not singled out as a destination.
objection: None beyond the list mention.

name: Talijancich
reason: Brief winery rule: a cellar door in a bare Wikivoyage list, not singled out as a destination.
objection: Known for fortified wines; still one of dozens.

name: Carilley Estate
reason: Brief winery rule: a cellar door in a bare Wikivoyage list, not singled out as a destination.
objection: None beyond the list mention.

name: The Olive Farm
reason: Brief winery rule: a cellar door/farm shop in a bare Wikivoyage list, not singled out as a destination.
objection: None beyond the list mention.

name: Feral Brewing
reason: Brief brewery rule: a brewery taproom in a bare Wikivoyage list; no source singles it out as a destination in its own right.
objection: A well-known craft brewery among beer travellers; still a bar/restaurant venue.

name: Lancaster Wines
reason: Brief winery rule: a cellar door in a bare Wikivoyage list, not singled out as a destination.
objection: None beyond the list mention.

name: Garbin Estate
reason: Brief winery rule: a cellar door in a bare Wikivoyage list, not singled out as a destination.
objection: None beyond the list mention.

name: Jane Brook Estate
reason: Brief winery rule: a cellar door in a bare Wikivoyage list, not singled out as a destination.
objection: None beyond the list mention.

name: Edgecombe Wines
reason: Brief winery rule: a family cafe and cellar door (Wikivoyage Eat listing 'Edgecombe Brothers'); no source singles it out as a destination.
objection: Wikivoyage gives it an Eat entry, i.e. a restaurant.

name: Henley Park
reason: Brief winery rule: a cellar door in a bare Wikivoyage list, not singled out as a destination. (Candidate coordinates are Henley Park in England.)
objection: None beyond the list mention.

name: Wild Swan
reason: Rule: a winery, brewery or shop is a place only when a visitor source singles it out as a destination; Wikivoyage Perth/Swan Valley only lists it by name in a bare list of cellar doors along West Swan Road, with no description.
objection: It is a real cellar door a visitor can drink at, but nothing marks it out from dozens of others.

name: Black Swan
reason: Rule: a winery, brewery or shop is a place only when a visitor source singles it out as a destination; Wikivoyage Perth/Swan Valley only lists it by name in a bare list of cellar doors along West Swan Road, with no description.
objection: As for Wild Swan: open to visitors, but one name in a list of cellar doors.

name: Margaret River Chocolate Factory (Swan Valley)
reason: Rule 2: a shop (chocolate factory shop and café), named only in the Wikivoyage Swan Valley bare list; not a place in its own right.
objection: Free tastings make it a popular family stop in the Swan Valley; a regional board page might single it out.

name: Sandalford Wines
reason: Rule: a winery, brewery or shop is a place only when a visitor source singles it out as a destination; Wikivoyage Perth/Swan Valley only lists it by name in a bare list of cellar doors along West Swan Road, with no description. Sandalford is one of WA's oldest estates (has a Wikipedia article, 1,606 views), but no counted source singles it out.
objection: Strongest of the wineries: an 1840 landmark estate with tours; if a Tourism WA or Destination Perth page names it as a destination it would reach review.

name: Lilac Hill Estate
reason: Rule: a winery, brewery or shop is a place only when a visitor source singles it out as a destination; Wikivoyage Perth/Swan Valley only lists it by name in a bare list of cellar doors along West Swan Road, with no description.
objection: One name in a list; the separate Lilac Hill Park picnic spot (Destination Perth) is a different place.

name: Ironbark Brewery
reason: Rule: a winery, brewery or shop is a place only when a visitor source singles it out as a destination; Wikivoyage Perth/Swan Valley only lists it by name in a bare list of cellar doors along West Swan Road, with no description.
objection: Open brewery venue, but one name in a list.

name: Riverbank Estate
reason: Rule: a winery, brewery or shop is a place only when a visitor source singles it out as a destination; Wikivoyage Perth/Swan Valley only lists it by name in a bare list of cellar doors along West Swan Road, with no description.
objection: Open cellar door, but one name in a list.

name: Mundaring Weir
reason: Rules 1-4: Wikivoyage Perth/The Hills See listing (walk over the weir, picnic areas, museum) and Destination Perth (Perth Hills and Mundaring pages: "Explore the Mundaring Weir and No 1 Pump Station"). Open access, an hour or more.
objection: Lake C. Y. O'Connor is the same reservoir: keep one spot (this one), not both.

name: Kalamunda Zig Zag Trail
reason: Rules 1-3: Wikivoyage Perth/The Hills See listing, a popular scenic drive (also walkable) on a converted rail line with views over Perth; a distinct Perth Hills icon.
objection: Only one counted source and the listing's link is dead; it is a drive of 15-20 minutes. Check the gates/one-way hours before writing hours.

name: Railway Reserve Heritage Trail
reason: Rules 1-3: Wikivoyage Perth/The Hills Do listing and Destination Perth (Perth Hills: "Walk the Railway Reserves Heritage Trail"; Mundaring and Kalamunda pages). Open-access walk and ride trail.
objection: A long loop trail that visitors join at any point; pin needs the midpoint of the route. Name is "Railway Reserves Heritage Trail" in the board's spelling.

name: Lesmurdie Falls
reason: Rules 1-3: Wikivoyage Perth/The Hills See listing ("one of the more spectacular waterfalls on the Darling Range escarpment") and Destination Perth Kalamunda page (lookouts at Lesmurdie Falls). Open access.
objection: Flows only after winter rain; in summer it is a dry rock face with a city view.

name: Rocky Pool
reason: Rule 1: Wikivoyage Perth/The Hills mentions Rocky Pool in Swan View as a start of the Railway Reserves Heritage Trail; DBCA Kalamunda National Park lists a "Rocky Pool" attraction (on Piesse Brook). Case for: a natural swimming hole named by two sources.
objection: The two sources may be two different Rocky Pools (Swan View/John Forrest vs Kalamunda NP); the Wikivoyage mention is only a trail access point, not a listing. Confirm which one and its coordinates before keeping.

name: Goat Farm Mountain Bike Park
reason: Rule 1: Wikivoyage Perth/The Hills (Do: mountain biking) names it; Trails WA carries it as a trail (Greenmount). Case for: a real open-access mountain bike park in the hills.
objection: Mostly used by local riders who bring their own bikes; a passing mention in one counted source; closer to "a place only locals use" than a visitor draw.

name: Mount Dale
reason: Rules 1-3: DBCA Helena National Park page calls it "the park's major attraction accessible by road", with panoramic views over the Darling Range, and a Bibbulmun Track drop-off point; the Bibbulmun Track Foundation names it too.
objection: A drive-up lookout; the visit can be short unless combined with a walk.

name: Helena National Park
reason: Rule 1: DBCA visitor page (jarrah and wandoo forest, Bibbulmun Track). Case for: a national park with a visitor page and a road-access lookout.
objection: Its only named draw is Mount Dale, a separate candidate; without it the park is unmarked bush with no facilities. Keep one (Mount Dale) unless the park has another visitor point.

name: Kalamunda National Park
reason: Rule 1: DBCA visitor page; the Bibbulmun Track northern terminus and Piesse Brook walks start here. Case for: the start of WA's best-known long walk.
objection: No facilities; the draw is the Bibbulmun Track (a separate candidate) and the terminus in Kalamunda town. Near-duplicate of Bibbulmun Track and Kalamunda.

name: Lake Leschenaultia
reason: Rules 1-3: Wikivoyage Perth/Outer Perth See listing and Destination Perth Perth Hills page ("Enjoy a picnic, canoe or swim at Lake Leschenaultia"); swimming, canoeing, MTB trails.
objection: The Wikivoyage listing has no description; otherwise a clear day-trip lake.

name: Serpentine Falls
reason: Rules 1-3: Wikivoyage Perth/Outer Perth See listing and DBCA Serpentine National Park ("main attraction"). Open daily, picnic ground.
objection: Water flows mainly in autumn and winter; park entry fee.

name: Serpentine National Park
reason: Rules 1-3: DBCA visitor page (Serpentine Falls, Kitty's Gorge Walk Trail, Baldwin's Bluff Nature Track, wildflowers) and Destination Perth Perth Hills page (Serpentine-Jarrahdale: forests and walking tracks).
objection: Its headline is Serpentine Falls, a separate spot: the park must take a different visitor point (Kitty's Gorge or Baldwin's Bluff) and photo, or the two are near-duplicates.

name: Mount Cooke
reason: Rules 1-3: re-looked for a counted source: the Bibbulmun Track Foundation's Darling Range page names Mt Cooke (582 m, the highest point in the Darling Range, outstanding views) and the Shire of Wandering publishes a Mount Cooke Trail walk page (11 km, about 4 hours from the Sullivan Rock car park). A summit day walk in Monadnocks Conservation Park.
objection: Part of the Bibbulmun Track (a candidate itself); keep only as a named day section. Pin on the summit, not the car park on Albany Highway.

name: Bibbulmun Track
reason: Rules 1-3: DBCA (Kalamunda NP: "this is where the Bibbulmun Track starts"), the Bibbulmun Track Foundation, and Destination Perth (Perth Hills, Dwellingup pages: "iconic"). WA's flagship long-distance walk, open all year.
objection: 1,000 km long and runs through three regions; the proposer must pin it once (its centre) and not duplicate it in the South West and Great Southern passes.

name: Lake C. Y. O'Connor
reason: Rule 3: duplicate of Mundaring Weir. It is the reservoir behind the weir; Wikivoyage Perth mentions it only as 'Mundaring Weir/Lake C Y O'Connor' (kangaroos near the car park).
objection: The kangaroos and lake views are a reason to stop, but the place is the same as Mundaring Weir.

name: Kalamunda
reason: Town rule: Destination Perth gives it its own page (Kalamunda History Village, Zig Zag Cultural Centre, heritage walk, Bibbulmun northern terminus) and Wikivoyage Perth/The Hills covers it; a base for the Perth Hills.
objection: Its Sunday farmers market is a weekly event and not a reason; the town may be filed under Perth.

name: Mundaring
reason: Town rule, re-looked for a counted source: Destination Perth has its own Mundaring page (visitor centre, Mundaring Weir, Perth Hills Discovery Centre, Railway Reserves Heritage Trail).
objection: Most of its draws (the weir, the heritage trail) are separate candidates; the town itself is a village strip with a visitor centre, close to a wrapper for its attractions.

name: Boyagin Rock
reason: Outside the region: belongs to wa-golden-outback (DBCA places Boyagin Nature Reserve in Australia's Golden Outback, Narrogin office; Wheatbelt, Shire of Brookton/Pingelly, not the Avon Valley list).
objection: DBCA does describe it as a climbable granite outcrop with views, so the Golden Outback pass should consider it.

name: Giants of Mandurah
reason: Rules 1-3: Wikivoyage Mandurah See listing and Destination Perth Mandurah page ("world-class outdoor sculpture trail"); Visit Mandurah calls it a must-do. Free, open access, a half day to see them all.
objection: Five sculptures spread across the region: it is a trail, not one point; pin and bio must say so.

name: Mandurah Museum
reason: Rule 1: Wikivoyage Mandurah See listing only ("small local history museum", gold-coin donation). Case for: open to the public, about an hour.
objection: One counted source, a small local museum; fails the friend test unless already in Mandurah.

name: Amaze Miniature Park
reason: Rule 1: Wikivoyage Mandurah See listing (Wed-Sat 10-4:30). Case for: a family attraction a guide names.
objection: One counted source with a one-word description; opens four days a week; a local family attraction.

name: Mandjar Bay
reason: Rule 1: Wikivoyage Mandurah names Mandjar Bay as the base for dolphin tours; Visit Mandurah lists it as one of the best places to see dolphins. Case for: dolphins are seen from the shore here, on the town's waterfront.
objection: It is Mandurah's foreshore and marina where tours leave from (a tour base, not a draw of its own), so it may be a near-duplicate of Mandurah itself.

name: Lake Clifton Thrombolites
reason: Rules 1-3: Wikivoyage Mandurah See listing and DBCA Yalgorup National Park (boardwalk to the thrombolites, "ancient living rock legends"). Open access boardwalk.
objection: A short boardwalk visit (20-30 min); overlaps Yalgorup NP, whose headline it is.

name: Yalgorup National Park
reason: Rules 1-3: DBCA visitor page (ten Ramsar lakes, Heathlands Walk Trail, Martins Tank campground) and Destination Perth Waroona page (tuart trees, thrombolites, Heathlands Trail over Lake Preston).
objection: Its best-known draw is the Lake Clifton Thrombolites, a separate spot: the park must take a different visitor point (Heathlands Walk / Martins Tank).

name: Dwellingup
reason: Town rule, re-looked for a counted source: Tourism WA has a Dwellingup place page ("Dwellingup Trail Town") and Destination Perth its own Dwellingup page (Lane Poole Reserve, Bibbulmun Track, Munda Biddi, Hotham Valley Railway, Treetops Adventure). A base visitors stay in.
objection: Many of its draws lie in Lane Poole Reserve outside town.

name: Hotham Valley Railway
reason: "A spot is a place": a heritage railway whose rides run between Pinjarra and Dwellingup, both of which are candidates; the ride belongs in the Dwellingup (or Pinjarra) bio and ticketUrl.
objection: Destination Perth names it ("Hop aboard the Hotham Valley Tourist Railway") and the ride is itself the attraction for many; the forest steam ride could be argued as a ride-is-the-attraction exception.

name: Munda Biddi Trail
reason: Rules 1-3, re-looked for a counted source: Australia's South West board listing (australiassouthwest.com/listings/munda-biddi-trail), Destination Perth Dwellingup and Waroona pages, and Wikivoyage Perth/The Hills (Do: mountain biking). A 1,000 km off-road cycle trail from Mundaring to Albany.
objection: Spans three regions like the Bibbulmun; pin once at its centre and do not duplicate it in other region passes.

name: Captain Fawcett 4WD Trail
reason: Rule 1: DBCA site page (four-wheel-drive track through jarrah forest) and Trails WA (40 km, Dwellingup to Quindanning). Case for: a named agency-promoted route.
objection: Only for experienced 4WD drivers with their own vehicle; Trails WA says it is currently impassable and closed for winter; a vehicle route rather than a place most visitors go.

name: Pinjarra
reason: Town rule, re-looked for a counted source: Destination Perth has its own Pinjarra page (1.3 km heritage trail past 19 historic sites from Edenvale Heritage Precinct, Murray River, Exchange Hotel tour).
objection: A small town 20 minutes from Mandurah; its events (Pinjarra Festival) are not reasons.

name: Waroona
reason: Town rule: Destination Perth has a Shire of Waroona page, but its draws are Waroona Dam, Drakesbrook Weir, Lane Poole, Yalgorup and Preston Beach, not the town; the town gets only "experience the charm of Waroona's town centre" and a visitor centre with a gallery. Case for: a highway town with a visitor centre.
objection: A shire page, not the town: a town with nothing of its own named to see. Waroona Dam or Drakesbrook Weir may be the real candidates.

name: Moore River National Park
reason: Rule 1: no counted source found on a re-look (no DBCA visitor page: its URL is a 404; Wikipedia says there are no facilities). Rule 2: banksia heath with no visitor access point.
objection: Known for Christmas-tree and verticordia wildflowers in a DBCA Landscope article; Guilderton's Moore River (Destination Perth) is a different place.

name: Gingin
reason: Town rule, re-looked for a counted source: Destination Perth "Gingin & Guilderton" page (historic town around Gingin Brook, Granville Park, walking trails, heritage).
objection: Its standout draw is the Gravity Discovery Centre outside town, which should be its own spot; the town itself is a short stop.

name: Beverley
reason: Town rule, re-looked for a counted source: Destination Perth Avon Valley page gives Beverley its own section (one of WA's first towns, colonial architecture, heritage). (Wikivoyage "Beverley" is the English town, not this one.)
objection: A small Avon Valley town; its August festival is not a reason, and York nearby is the stronger base.

name: Rockingham
reason: Town rule, re-looked for a counted source: Wikivoyage has a full Rockingham (Western Australia) town article and Destination Perth its own Rockingham page; the base for Penguin Island and the Shoalwater Islands.
objection: Visitors may file it under Perth; most draws (Penguin Island, Point Peron) are separate spots.

name: Rockingham Beach
reason: Rules 1-3: Wikivoyage Rockingham See listing ("the best, and busiest beach in the city", the only north-facing beach in the Perth region) and Destination Perth Rockingham page (sheltered for families, Churchill Park dive trail).
objection: A city beach beside the foreshore; may read as part of Rockingham itself.

name: Penguin Island
reason: Rules 1-3: Wikivoyage Rockingham See listing (little penguin colony, walking trails, ferry from Mersey Point) and Destination Perth ("Visit Penguin Island/Goolidja Goorda"). The island is the spot, not the ferry.
objection: Closed in part of the year for penguin breeding (check the season for hours).

name: Point Peron
reason: Rules 1-3: Wikivoyage Rockingham See listing (beaches, trails, WWII ruins) and Destination Perth ("Point Peron's scenic trails and lookout"); DBCA calls Cape Peron the hub of Rockingham Lakes Regional Park.
objection: None strong; overlaps the Shoalwater Islands Marine Park candidate.

name: Lake Richmond
reason: Rules 1-3: Wikivoyage Rockingham See listing (one of only two places in WA to see thrombolites) and DBCA Rockingham Lakes Regional Park ("star attraction of the park"). Open access viewing points.
objection: Near-duplicate in kind of the Lake Clifton Thrombolites, which are better known; a short visit.

name: Rockingham Museum
reason: Rules 1-3: Wikivoyage Rockingham See listing (local history in the historic Road Board building, about an hour) and Destination Perth Rockingham page (Art Deco building, interactive displays). Two counted sources.
objection: A small local-history museum open only four afternoons a week; fails the friend test unless already in Rockingham, so it could fairly sit at review.

name: Mandurah Hill
reason: Rule 1: Wikivoyage Rockingham See listing only ("wonderful look out with excellent views", Golden Bay). Case for: a free lookout a guide names.
objection: One counted source, a suburban dune lookout with a short visit; no tourism board mention found.

name: Rockingham Waterfront Village
reason: Rules 2-4: a dining and shopping precinct whose Wikivoyage mention is as the venue for festivals (International Food Festival, Cast Aways); the beach beside it is the Rockingham Beach spot.
objection: Destination Perth does mention waterfront cafés along the Rockingham Foreshore; it could be read as the town's foreshore.

name: Shoalwater Islands Marine Park
reason: Rule 1: DBCA visitor page (snorkelling, dive wreck, kayak tours to Seal Island with sea lions, boardwalks) and Destination Perth Rockingham page. Case for: two counted sources and a real range of water activities.
objection: Rule 3: an area containing Penguin Island, Seal Island and Point Peron, which are separate spots; much of what it offers is tours. Better as the context in those bios than as its own spot.

name: Marmion Marine Park
reason: Rule 1: DBCA visitor page (reefs, Boyinaboat Reef dive trail off Hillarys, Mettam's Pool, whale watching). Case for: a named marine park with shore-access diving.
objection: Rule 3: an area whose visitor points are Mettam's Pool and Hillarys Boat Harbour, which are separate candidates; most of it needs a boat or charter.

name: Mettam's Pool
reason: Rules 1-3: Wikivoyage Perth/The Coast See listing, DBCA Marmion Marine Park ("safe snorkelling close to shore") and Destination Perth Sunset Coast ("the best snorkeling spot in Perth"). Open access.
objection: A small lagoon; conditions depend on swell.

name: Swanbourne Beach
reason: Rules 1-3: Wikivoyage Perth/The Coast See listing (Perth's only clothing-optional beach, 500 m north of the main beach). Second-tier beach a guide names.
objection: One counted source; its draw is niche, and Cottesloe next door is the main beach.

name: Scarborough Beach
reason: Rules 1-3: Wikivoyage Perth/The Coast See listing, Destination Perth's own Scarborough Beach page ("one of Perth's most popular seaside destinations"; skate park, surf). Open access.
objection: None strong.

name: Scarborough Sunset Markets
reason: Rule 4: a weekly market (Thursday evenings in summer, Saturdays in winter); belongs in Scarborough Beach's text, not a spot.
objection: Wikivoyage and Destination Perth both promote it.

name: Trigg Point
reason: Rule 3: duplicate of Trigg Beach: the surf break at the point of Trigg Beach; Destination Perth names it only in a list of surf spots.
objection: It is the named surf break surfers seek out; could be kept as the beach under the name "Trigg Point" if preferred.

name: Strickland Bay
reason: Rule 1: Destination Perth names it only in a list of surf spots (Rottnest Island's main surf break). Case for: a named bay on Rottnest that surfers go to.
objection: A passing mention in a surf list; Wikivoyage Rottnest Island does not name it; one of many Rottnest bays and a ride from the settlement.

name: Trigg Beach
reason: Rules 1-3, re-looked for a counted source: Wikivoyage Perth/The Coast (Do: surf "you should be able to find a wave on Trigg Beach") and Destination Perth (Sunset Coast and Scarborough Beach pages: "Perth's most consistent surf break"). Keep as one spot with Trigg Point.
objection: Close to Scarborough Beach (about 2 km) and could be read as its northern extension.

name: Hillarys Boat Harbour
reason: Rule 1+2: Wikivoyage Perth/The Coast Do listing (marina with sheltered swimming beach, boardwalk) and Destination Perth's beaches guide names it a coastal tourist hub; free, open any time, an hour or more on the boardwalk and beach.
objection: Largely a marina of restaurants and shops (a 'plain shops/restaurants' venue); AQWA next door may be the real draw and the two sit 300 m apart, so placement must keep them distinct.

name: The Great Escape Water Park
reason: Rule 3: a small commercial water park (three slides, mini golf, trampolines) inside Hillarys Boat Harbour; part of that larger spot and a business rather than a place.
objection: Wikivoyage does list it under Do, and it is a ticketed attraction families go to; could be mentioned in Hillarys Boat Harbour's bio.

name: Aquarium of Western Australia
reason: Rule 1+2: Wikivoyage Perth/The Coast See listing (underwater tunnel, open daily 10-5, paid entry); the state's main aquarium, a 1-2 hour visit.
objection: One counted source in the shard; next to Hillarys Boat Harbour, so the two must not be merged or share a pin.

name: Sculptures by the Sea
reason: Rule 4: an annual autumn exhibition on Cottesloe Beach (Wikivoyage calls it an annual exposition), not there whenever you arrive.
objection: Draws tens of thousands; belongs in Cottesloe Beach's description or a tip, not as a spot.

name: Floreat Beach
reason: Rule 1: Destination Perth's 'Best Beaches in Perth' names it among the Sunset Coast beaches and Tourism WA's City Beach page mentions the promenade linking to it; a patrolled swimming beach.
objection: Rule 3: it adjoins City Beach on one promenade and is only ever named in passing beside it; likely a near-duplicate of City Beach.

name: City Beach
reason: Rule 1+2: Tourism WA attraction page ('one of Perth's most popular coastal attractions'), Destination Perth beaches guide and Wikivoyage Perth/The Coast intro; groyne-sheltered patrolled swimming beach.
objection: Script found no counted source (it had none attached); now two. One of many metro beaches; neighbours Floreat Beach.

name: Como Beach
reason: Rule 1: no counted source found (Wikivoyage Perth districts, Destination Perth beaches guides and Tourism WA beaches page do not name it); a local Swan River beach in Como.
objection: Has a Wikipedia article and is a calm river swim; if a board page turns up it could be reconsidered.

name: North Beach
reason: Rule 1: Destination Perth's beaches guide names North Beach in its Sunset Coast list; an open beach on the coastal path.
objection: Named only in a list, with nothing said about it; one weak counted source for a suburban beach near better-known Trigg and Scarborough.

name: Peppermint Grove Beach
reason: Outside the region: belongs to wa-south-west (the coordinates, -33.52 115.51, are the Capel coast south of Bunbury, not Perth).
objection: None for this region; the wa-south-west pass should judge it.

name: C.Y. O'Connor Beach
reason: Rule 1: Destination Perth's Fremantle beaches guide names O'Connor Reserve as a dog-friendly beach; the beach is known for the C.Y. O'Connor statue standing in the water.
objection: Rule 1: the mention is a passing one for a dog beach; no counted source describes the statue or the beach as a place to go. Mainly local use.

name: Sunset Beach, Western Australia
reason: Outside the region: belongs to wa-coral-coast (coordinates -28.72 114.62 are Geraldton).
objection: None for this region.

name: Bicton Baths
reason: Rule 1+2: DBCA Explore Parks has a site page (Swan Canning Riverpark) for swimming, canoeing and walking at this 1926 river baths; free, open access.
objection: Rule 'places only locals use': a neighbourhood river swimming spot with one agency page and no tourism-board listing.

name: Twilight Hawkers Market
reason: Rule 4: a Friday-night food market running October to April only (Wikivoyage Perth), a weekly seasonal market.
objection: Popular with visitors; belongs in Perth's tips, not as a spot.

name: Mandurah Crab Fest
reason: Rule 4: an annual festival on the third weekend of March (Wikivoyage Mandurah).
objection: None: an event.

name: York Motor Museum
reason: Rule 1+2: Wikivoyage York See listing (daily 9-4, about 90 vehicles, paid entry) and Destination Perth's York page and Avon Valley road trip; a 1 hour museum visit.
objection: A community-run museum in a country town; Destination Perth's 'only community-owned motor museum in Australia' claim is unverified.

name: Residency Museum, York
reason: Rule 1+2: Wikivoyage York See listing (1850s convict-depot residence, local history museum) and Destination Perth's York page ('well worth a visit').
objection: Opens only Fri 1-3 and weekends 11-3 (volunteer-run), so many visitors find it shut; a small local museum.

name: Holy Trinity Church, York
reason: Rule 2 (church rule): Wikivoyage York gives only its date and convict builders and where it stands; no source names an interior, art or tour to see.
objection: A convict-built 1855 church on York's heritage walk; if a source named its interior (e.g. stained glass) it could be reviewed.

name: St Patrick's Church, York
reason: Rule 2 (church rule): Wikivoyage York gives its history (convict architect Joseph Nunan) but names nothing to see or do inside, and no opening.
objection: Victorian Gothic church with an interesting story; a stop on a heritage walk at most.

name: York Suspension Bridge
reason: Rule 1+3: Wikivoyage York See listing and Destination Perth's Avon Valley road trip ('cross the river by suspension bridge'); a footbridge over the Avon by Holy Trinity.
objection: Rule 3: a few minutes' walk across, and it is a 1988 rebuild; better as part of York town's bio than a spot of its own.

name: Mount Brown Lookout
reason: Rule 1+2: Wikivoyage York See listing and Destination Perth's Avon Valley road trip ('360 degree panoramic view of York', free barbecue, picnic area); open 24 hours.
objection: A drive-up lookout; a short visit unless picnicking.

name: Avon Terrace
reason: Rule 1: Wikivoyage York names the main street lined with 19th-century buildings, and Destination Perth's York page describes its heritage streetscape and walking trails.
objection: Rule 3: it is York's town centre itself; if York is listed (as a town or destination) this is a near-duplicate and belongs in York's description.

name: Toodyay
reason: Towns rule: Wikivoyage has its own Toodyay page, Destination Perth a Toodyay page and Tourism WA a destination page; historic Avon Valley town with museums, heritage walk and Bilya Walk Track.
objection: The town's draws (Connor's Mill, Newcastle Gaol) are candidates too, so the proposer must avoid listing the town as a wrapper around them.

name: Connor's Mill
reason: Rule 1+2: Wikivoyage Toodyay See listing (1875 mill, working order, daily 10-3:30, $3), Tourism WA attraction page 'Connor's Mill Museum' and Destination Perth's Toodyay page.
objection: A small three-storey museum; about half an hour.

name: Newcastle Gaol Museum
reason: Rule 1+2: Wikivoyage Toodyay See listing (1865 gaol, daily 10-3, paid) and Destination Perth's Toodyay page and Avon Valley road trip (where the Moondyne Joe legend began).
objection: A small local museum; about half an hour.

name: Pelham Reserve
reason: Rule 1: Wikivoyage Toodyay See listing (wooded hill, Drummond memorial, WWI range, WWII bunker) and Destination Perth's Toodyay page and road trip (spring wildflowers, stargazing over town).
objection: Leave-out rule: an ordinary town reserve with picnic sites; mainly a local park, seasonally interesting for wildflowers.

name: St Stephen's Church, Toodyay
reason: Rule 2 (church rule): Wikivoyage says only that it is a small 1862 redbrick Anglican church still in use; nothing named to see inside.
objection: One of the first buildings in Toodyay, opposite Connor's Mill; a heritage walk stop.

name: St Philip's Church, Culham
reason: Rule 2 (church rule): Wikivoyage Toodyay gives only its location and 1857 date; a rural church with nothing named to see or do.
objection: Old (1857) and listed in a See section; nothing more.

name: Toodyay Miniature Railway
reason: Rule 2: closed (Wikivoyage: 'remains closed in 2023').
objection: Might reopen; recheck in a later pass.

name: Northam
reason: Towns rule: Wikivoyage Northam page and Tourism WA destination page; the Avon Valley's largest town with the suspension bridge, white swans and Bernard Park.
objection: Wikivoyage itself says the highway town lacks old-world ambiance; its main draw is Bernard Park's bridge, also a candidate, so avoid listing the town as a wrapper.

name: St John's Church, Northam
reason: Rule 2 (church rule): Wikivoyage lists opening hours (Fri-Mon 11-3) but names nothing to see; no other visitor source.
objection: It is open to visitors on set days, which suggests an interior; if a source named something there it could be reviewed.

name: Northam Heritage Forum
reason: Rule 1+2: Wikivoyage Northam See listing (old locomotives in a disused railway station, Fri-Mon 11-3).
objection: One counted source, a one-line listing; limited opening days; a small volunteer railway museum.

name: Mount Ommanney Lookout
reason: Rule 1: Wikivoyage Northam See listing (lookout reached by road or a hike).
objection: One counted source and a one-line mention; no tourism-board page found; a short-stop town lookout.

name: Northam Silos
reason: Rule 2: Wikivoyage says the painted silos cannot be properly seen without trespassing on an industrial site; no public access to view them.
objection: Silo art is a WA roadside icon type; if a public viewing point exists it could be revisited.

name: Bernard Park
reason: Rule 1+2: Wikivoyage Northam See listing, and Tourism WA attraction pages for Bernard Park and for its Suspension Bridge (one of Australia's longest pedestrian suspension bridges; white swans); free, open any time, a riverside walk circuit.
objection: Its headline is the bridge; the spot should be named for what visitors come for (park plus bridge), and it is a short visit.

name: New Norcia
reason: Towns rule / rule 1: Wikivoyage Wheatbelt lists it as 'Australia's only monastic town'; a Benedictine monastery town with museum, art gallery and town tours, open to visitors.
objection: Wikivoyage's own page redirects to the Wheatbelt region (one line); a richer counted source (the town's visitor centre or Tourism WA) should be attached by the proposer.

name: Yanchep National Park
reason: Rule 1+2: DBCA Explore Parks park page (koala boardwalk, kangaroos, caves on guided tours, trails, Wangi Mia Aboriginal experience, visitor centre).
objection: None of substance; the koala and cave candidates are parts of this park.

name: Crystal Caves
reason: Rule 1+2+3: DBCA Yanchep page ('Explore Crystal or Yonderup Cave on a guided tour') with its own Crystal Cave attraction tile; a ticketed guided tour, distinct from the park's picnic areas.
objection: Rule 3: it lies inside Yanchep National Park and might be better as a line in the park's bio; name is 'Crystal Cave' on DBCA, not 'Caves'.

name: Yonderup Cave
reason: Rule 1: DBCA Yanchep page names it as a guided-tour cave alongside Crystal Cave.
objection: Rule 3: a second cave in the same park, toured less often than Crystal Cave; likely a near-duplicate of the Crystal Cave spot.

name: Yanchep Koala Boardwalk
reason: Rule 3: part of Yanchep National Park (DBCA describes the koala boardwalk as one of the park's features beside the main picnic area); a short stroll, not a separate place.
objection: It is the park's headline experience for many visitors; if the park is not kept as a spot this should be.

name: Elizabeth Quay
reason: Rule 1+2: Destination Perth's 'Things to Do at Elizabeth Quay: Complete Guide' (riverside precinct, bridge, Island playground, ferry jetty) ; free, open any time, an hour's wander.
objection: Script found no counted source (Wikivoyage mentions it only for transport); largely a dining and transport hub.

name: Matilda Bay
reason: Rule 1: DBCA's 'Enjoy nature in Perth' says to relax at Matilda Bay Reserve, grassy riverside parkland facing Perth city and Kings Park.
objection: One counted source, a passing mention; a riverside picnic reserve that locals use more than visitors; near Kings Park.

name: London Court
reason: Rule 1: Visit Perth (City of Perth) lists it as a 1937 Tudor-style heritage arcade; Tourism WA lists laneway walking tours that feature it.
objection: Rule 2: it is a shopping arcade, which the rule fails as a shop venue; it is a quick photo stop on the way between Hay Street Mall and St Georges Terrace.

name: His Majesty's Theatre
reason: Rule 2: a performance venue (Wikivoyage Perth mentions it only as where WA Opera and Ballet perform); nothing to do there without a show ticket.
objection: Historic 1904 Edwardian theatre; if a source named regular public tours it could be reviewed.

name: St Mary's Cathedral, Perth
reason: Rule 2 (church rule satisfied): Tourism WA attraction page describes what to see (the 1865 nave joined to a modern curved extension and second spire) and says it is open daily to visitors.
objection: One counted source; a working cathedral that is not a headline Perth sight.

name: Araluen Botanic Park
reason: Rule 1+2: Destination Perth attraction listing and Perth Hills pages; a 59 ha paid botanic park with camellia and heritage rose collections, open daily.
objection: Its fame is the spring tulip festival (an event); outside August-October it is a quieter garden.

name: Herdsman Lake
reason: Rule 1+2: DBCA park page for Herdsman Lake Regional Park (birdwatching wetland, Discovery Centre, walk and cycle trails), free.
objection: Leave-out rule: an urban wetland park mainly used by local walkers and birders; one agency source, no tourism-board listing found.

name: Carnac Island
reason: Rule 1+2: Tourism WA attraction page and DBCA Carnac Island Nature Reserve page; a day-trip island off Fremantle where Australian sea lions haul out, reached by boat, with swimming and snorkelling.
objection: Access is limited: boat only, visitors must stay on the beach (tiger snakes), and DBCA restricts beach access November-March; operators sell the trips.

name: Garden Island
reason: Rule 2: an active naval base (HMAS Stirling); Wikivoyage Rockingham says only parts can be reached by private boat in daylight with restrictions; no visitor source names it as a place to go.
objection: Recreational boaters do anchor at its bays; high page views.

name: Leighton Beach
reason: Rule 1+2: Destination Perth's Fremantle beaches guide (picturesque, fine white sand, swimming and kitesurfing) and Wikivoyage Perth/The Coast (reached from North Fremantle station, surfing); free.
objection: Second-tier city beach; near Cottesloe.

name: Sorrento Beach
reason: Rule 1+2: Tourism WA attraction page and Destination Perth listing (netted swimming enclosure, reef, picnic area), and Wikivoyage Perth/The Coast names it as a notable beach.
objection: Beside Hillarys Boat Harbour; one of many metro beaches.

name: Heirisson Island
reason: Rule 1+2: Wikivoyage Perth/City See listing (wild kangaroos roam the island in the Swan River, free, reached from the Causeway); a distinct wildlife stop in the city.
objection: Wikivoyage says there are only five or six kangaroos, often hiding; a short visit that can disappoint.

name: Crown Perth
reason: Rule 2 / business rule: a casino and hotel complex (Wikivoyage lists it as an entertainment precinct of casino, theatre, bars); a venue that is a business, not a place to see.
objection: Wikivoyage does list it under See; many visitors go for shows.

name: Claisebrook Cove
reason: Rule 1: Wikivoyage Perth/City See listing ('spend an hour or so wandering' the architecture; footbridge views of the city at night).
objection: One counted source; an urban redevelopment and dining precinct that few visitor sources treat as a sight.

name: Kangaroos in the City
reason: Quirky landmark rule: Wikivoyage Perth/City See listing (larger-than-life bronze kangaroos, 'a magnet for international visitors'), free, always there.
objection: A short photo stop (0-15 min) on a city corner; one counted source.

name: Swan River
reason: Rule 3: a river running through the whole metro area is an area, not a place to go; its visitor points (Elizabeth Quay, Kings Park, Heirisson Island, Matilda Bay, foreshore paths) are the spots, and cruises are operators.
objection: Wikivoyage praises the riverside bike paths; the river is Perth's defining feature, so it belongs in Perth's description.
